newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK FIRMER ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS WEEK FIRMER ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar went into the weekend firmer against hard currencies after a fairly quiet Friday interbank session, dealers said.
They said the central Reserve Bank intervened in the morning to support the local currency against slight import pressure, pouring in slightly more money than was needed to cater for the demand.
"I think maybe the central bank thought there was too much pressure on the Zimbabwe dollar of late," one dealer suggested, echoing sentiments expressed by a colleague in the morning.
Despite it's depreciatory trend of the past week, dealers however expect the dollar to start appreciating on the back of export inflows from annual tobacco sales which opened in April.

Last week, one dealer suggested some tobacco producers could be holding back their proceeds from the auctions to allow the local currency to fall further so they could make a higher profit on their foreign currency.
At Friday's close, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 11.3150/3250 against the U.S. unit, up from 11.3275/3375 previously.

On the crosses, it strengthened to 18.2300/2500 from 18.4870/5090 versus sterling, tracking a firmer U.S. dollar overseas, and was at 6.5500/5700 against the mark from 6.5760/5840. It was also quoted firmer on South Africa's rand at 2.5400/5600 compared to 2.5460/5660.
